title: Warhammer 40,000 Roleplay Factions
description: Faction reference for a Warhammer 40k tabletop roleplaying campaign: lore, playstyle, goals and troop types.

categories.name: Xenos
categories.about: Alien species that the Imperium considers abominations to be purged. Each pursues its own ancient agenda, and many predate humanity by millions of years.

factions.name: Necrons
factions.about: An ancient race of skeletal androids who once ruled the galaxy as the Necrontyr. After trading their flesh for undying metal bodies, they slept for sixty million years in stasis-tombs. Now their dynasties are awakening to reclaim the stars.
lore: The Necrontyr were short-lived beings who allied with the star-gods known as the C'tan, who transferred their minds into living metal through biotransference.
During the Great Sundering the Necrons turned on the C'tan, shattering them into countless shards that are now bound as weapons.
Most rank-and-file Necrons lost their minds in the process; only the nobility retained their full personalities.
Many tomb worlds awoke damaged, leaving some Necron lords insane, such as those afflicted by the Flayer Virus.
factions.playstyle: Slow, relentless and extremely durable. Necron forces advance steadily, shrug off damage, and repair fallen warriors through Reanimation Protocols. In a roleplay setting they suit cold, calculating, aristocratic characters bound by ancient codes of honor.
goals: Reclaim their lost empire and the worlds they once ruled
Restore the dynasties and their former glory
Some nobles seek a way to return to flesh bodies
Eliminate the threat of the Tyranids and other upstart races

troops.name: Necron Warriors
troops.role: Core infantry armed with gauss flayers that strip targets apart atom by atom.

troops.name: Immortals
troops.role: Elite line troops who kept more of their minds and wield gauss blasters or tesla carbines.

troops.name: Lychguard
troops.role: Bodyguards of the nobility, armed with warscythes or hyperphase swords.

troops.name: Crypteks
troops.role: Techno-sorcerers who command the forces of physics and time.

troops.name: Overlords and Lords
troops.role: Noble commanders who lead the dynasties.

troops.name: Canoptek Constructs
troops.role: Scarabs, Wraiths and Spyders that maintain the tomb worlds.

troops.name: Flayed Ones
troops.role: Insane Necrons cursed with a hunger for flesh.

troops.name: C'tan Shards
troops.role: Enslaved fragments of star-gods unleashed as living weapons.

factions.name: Orks
factions.about: A brutal, green-skinned warrior race that lives for battle. Orks are the most widespread xenos species in the galaxy, and when gathered in vast numbers under a mighty warboss they form a WAAAGH! capable of overrunning entire sectors.
lore: Orks were engineered as soldiers by the ancient Old Ones for their war against the Necrons.
Orks reproduce by spores, meaning that wherever they fight, more Orks eventually grow.
Their collective psychic field makes their beliefs real: a vehicle painted red really does go faster.
Orks grow larger and stronger the more they fight, and leadership goes to the biggest and toughest.
factions.playstyle: Loud, aggressive and chaotic. Orks overwhelm enemies with numbers and close-combat fury, backed by ramshackle but surprisingly effective technology. In a roleplay setting they reward bold, reckless and humorous characters who solve problems by charging at them.
goals: Find the biggest, best fight possible
Loot shiny gear and better weapons (and teef, the Ork currency)
Grow bigger and climb the hierarchy to become a Warboss
Launch a WAAAGH! across the stars

troops.name: Boyz
troops.role: The core mob of Ork infantry, fighting with choppas and sluggas.

troops.name: Gretchin (Grots)
troops.role: Small, cowardly servants used as fodder and labor.

troops.name: Nobz
troops.role: Bigger, tougher Orks who boss the Boyz around.

troops.name: Warboss
troops.role: The biggest and meanest Ork, leader of the warband.

troops.name: Meks
troops.role: Instinctive engineers who build guns, vehicles and gadgets.

troops.name: Painboyz
troops.role: Crude surgeons who perform 'enhancements' on other Orks.

troops.name: Weirdboyz
troops.role: Ork psykers who channel the raw energy of the WAAAGH!

troops.name: Stormboyz
troops.role: Jump-pack troops who launch themselves into battle.

troops.name: Speed Freeks
troops.role: Bikers and buggy drivers obsessed with going fast.

troops.name: Deff Dreads and Killa Kans
troops.role: Walking war machines piloted by Orks or Grots.

factions.name: T'au Empire
factions.about: A young, technologically advanced and expansionist empire that believes in the 'Greater Good'. The T'au unite their own castes and many conquered or allied alien races under a single philosophy of cooperation and shared purpose.
lore: T'au society is divided into five castes: Fire (warriors), Earth (builders), Water (diplomats), Air (pilots) and the mysterious Ethereals who lead them all.
The T'au have almost no presence in the Warp, making them highly resistant to psychic and daemonic influence.
Their empire grew in only a few thousand years, a heartbeat compared to other races.
Commander Farsight broke away from the Empire after discovering secrets about the Ethereals, forming the Farsight Enclaves.
factions.playstyle: Ranged, tactical and highly coordinated. T'au rely on superior firepower, markerlights, drones and battlesuits, avoiding melee whenever possible. In a roleplay setting they suit diplomats, idealists and disciplined soldiers who believe in a cause greater than themselves.
goals: Spread the Greater Good across the galaxy
Bring other races into the empire through diplomacy or force
Advance their technology and expand through Spheres of Expansion
Protect T'au worlds from the Imperium, Tyranids and Chaos

troops.name: Fire Warriors
troops.role: Core infantry armed with long-range pulse rifles and carbines.

troops.name: Pathfinders
troops.role: Scouts who mark targets with markerlights for the rest of the army.

troops.name: Stealth Suits
troops.role: Cloaked battlesuits used for infiltration and harassment.

troops.name: Crisis Battlesuits
troops.role: Versatile jet-pack battlesuits piloted by elite Fire caste warriors.

troops.name: Broadsides
troops.role: Heavy battlesuits carrying anti-armor railguns and missile systems.

troops.name: Riptide and Stormsurge
troops.role: Massive battlesuits and walking gun platforms.

troops.name: Drones
troops.role: Artificially intelligent support units providing shields, guns and sensors.

troops.name: Ethereals
troops.role: Spiritual leaders whose presence inspires all T'au.

troops.name: Kroot
troops.role: Avian mercenary auxiliaries who excel at close combat and tracking.

troops.name: Vespid Stingwings
troops.role: Insectoid auxiliaries who fly into battle with neutron blasters.

factions.name: Tyranids
factions.about: An extragalactic swarm of bio-engineered horrors that devours all biological matter in its path. Directed by a single gestalt consciousness called the Hive Mind, Tyranid Hive Fleets strip entire worlds to bare rock.
lore: Tyranids arrived from beyond the galaxy in vast Hive Fleets such as Behemoth, Kraken and Leviathan.
Every Tyranid organism is a tool of the Hive Mind, adapted to a specific purpose.
Genestealers infiltrate worlds ahead of the fleets, creating Genestealer Cults that weaken planets from within.
The Hive Mind casts a 'Shadow in the Warp' that blocks psychic communication and terrifies psykers.
After consuming a world, the Tyranids digest all its biomass in pools, leaving it lifeless.
factions.playstyle: Overwhelming swarms supported by giant monstrous creatures. Tyranids constantly adapt to their enemies and rely on synapse creatures to keep the lesser beasts in line. In a roleplay setting they are best used as a terrifying antagonist, or for horror-themed campaigns built around survival.
goals: Consume all biomass in the galaxy
Adapt and evolve by absorbing the genetic traits of prey
Expand the Hive Fleets to new worlds
Eliminate psychic resistance and threats to the swarm

troops.name: Termagants and Hormagaunts
troops.role: Swarms of small, expendable creatures that fight at range or in melee.

troops.name: Rippers
troops.role: Tiny worm-like creatures that consume everything in their path.

troops.name: Tyranid Warriors
troops.role: Mid-sized synapse creatures that lead the swarm.

troops.name: Genestealers
troops.role: Fast, deadly infiltrators with razor-sharp claws.

troops.name: Lictors
troops.role: Camouflaged stalker-assassins that hunt prey ahead of the swarm.

troops.name: Zoanthropes
troops.role: Floating psychic creatures that blast enemies with Warp energy.

troops.name: Carnifexes
troops.role: Living battering rams built to smash armor and fortifications.

troops.name: Hive Tyrants
troops.role: Massive synaptic leaders that channel the will of the Hive Mind.

troops.name: Trygons and Mawlocs
troops.role: Burrowing monsters that ambush from below the ground.

troops.name: Hierophants and Bio-Titans
troops.role: Colossal war-beasts used in the largest invasions.

categories.name: Chaos
categories.about: The Chaos Gods are entities of the Warp born from the emotions of mortals. Their followers include traitor Space Marines, cultists, mutants and daemons, all seeking to corrupt or destroy the Imperium. The four great powers are Khorne, Tzeentch, Nurgle and Slaanesh.

factions.name: Khorne
factions.about: The Blood God and Lord of Skulls, Khorne is the Chaos God of rage, war, bloodshed and martial honor. He cares not from where the blood flows, only that it flows.
lore: Khorne sits upon a Brass Throne atop a mountain of skulls in his realm within the Warp.
He despises sorcery and psykers, seeing magic as the coward's weapon.
The World Eaters Legion, led by the Daemon Primarch Angron, is Khorne's most devoted Traitor Legion.
Khorne is the eternal enemy of Slaanesh, as rage and excess are opposed.
His followers shout the cry 'Blood for the Blood God! Skulls for the Skull Throne!'
factions.playstyle: Pure close-combat aggression. Khornate forces charge headlong into melee, gaining strength as they kill and refusing to use psychic powers. In a roleplay setting they suit berserkers, warrior-champions and characters driven by fury or a hunger for honorable combat.
goals: Spill as much blood as possible in Khorne's name
Collect skulls for the Skull Throne
Prove themselves through combat against worthy foes
Earn daemonhood through endless slaughter

troops.name: Khorne Berzerkers
troops.role: Frenzied Chaos Space Marines who live only to kill in melee.

troops.name: World Eaters
troops.role: The Traitor Legion devoted to Khorne.

troops.name: Bloodletters
troops.role: Lesser daemons of Khorne armed with hellblades.

troops.name: Flesh Hounds
troops.role: Daemonic hunting beasts immune to sorcery.

troops.name: Bloodcrushers
troops.role: Bloodletters riding brass-and-iron Juggernauts.

troops.name: Bloodthirsters
troops.role: Greater Daemons of Khorne, towering winged killers.

troops.name: Skulltakers
troops.role: Champions who gather skulls of mighty foes.

troops.name: Cultists of Khorne
troops.role: Mortal followers who fight in bloody mobs.

factions.name: Tzeentch
factions.about: The Changer of Ways and Architect of Fate, Tzeentch is the Chaos God of change, hope, ambition, sorcery and scheming. His plots are so complex that even failure may be part of his plan.
lore: Tzeentch dwells within the Crystal Labyrinth, an ever-shifting maze within the Warp.
The Thousand Sons Legion, led by the Daemon Primarch Magnus the Red, serves Tzeentch.
Ahriman's Rubric of Ahriman turned most of the Thousand Sons into dust-filled suits of armor.
Tzeentch is the opposite of Nurgle, since change opposes stagnation.
His followers are often sorcerers seeking forbidden knowledge or power.
factions.playstyle: Psychic and ranged warfare built around sorcery and trickery. Tzeentchian forces rely on powerful psykers, warpfire and manipulation of fate. In a roleplay setting they suit schemers, sorcerers, manipulators and ambitious characters seeking knowledge at any price.
goals: Gain forbidden knowledge and secrets
Manipulate events and people across the galaxy
Bring change and upheaval to stable systems
Ascend to daemonhood through mastery of sorcery

troops.name: Thousand Sons
troops.role: The Traitor Legion of sorcerers devoted to Tzeentch.

troops.name: Rubric Marines
troops.role: Soulless warriors bound in armor, firing warpflame bolts.

troops.name: Scarab Occult Terminators
troops.role: Elite Terminator-armored Rubricae.

troops.name: Sorcerers
troops.role: Powerful psykers who command the Warp.

troops.name: Pink and Blue Horrors
troops.role: Lesser daemons who split apart when slain.

troops.name: Flamers of Tzeentch
troops.role: Daemons who spew multi-colored warpfire.

troops.name: Screamers
troops.role: Flying shark-like daemons that soar through the Warp.

troops.name: Lords of Change
troops.role: Greater Daemons of Tzeentch, bird-like masters of sorcery.

troops.name: Tzaangors
troops.role: Beastman-like mutants devoted to Tzeentch.

factions.name: Nurgle
factions.about: Grandfather Nurgle is the Chaos God of disease, decay, despair and rebirth. Surprisingly jovial, he loves his followers and gifts them with plagues that make them immune to pain and fear of death.
lore: Nurgle tends his Garden of Nurgle within the Warp, brewing new plagues in his great cauldron.
The Death Guard Legion, led by the Daemon Primarch Mortarion, serves Nurgle.
Nurgle offers comfort to those who despair over their mortality.
His followers are bloated, rotting and nearly unkillable.
Nurgle and Tzeentch are bitter rivals, as decay opposes change.
factions.playstyle: Slow, tough and grinding attrition warfare. Nurgle forces are extremely durable and spread disease to weaken enemies over time. In a roleplay setting they suit resilient, grim, oddly cheerful or fatalistic characters who embrace endurance.
goals: Spread plagues and disease across the galaxy
Expand the Garden of Nurgle into reality
Bring despair and decay to the living
Show mortals the 'gift' of Nurgle's love

troops.name: Death Guard
troops.role: The Traitor Legion devoted to Nurgle.

troops.name: Plague Marines
troops.role: Rotting Chaos Space Marines with toxic weapons.

troops.name: Blightlord Terminators
troops.role: Elite Terminators of the Death Guard.

troops.name: Poxwalkers
troops.role: Zombie-like victims of the Walking Pox.

troops.name: Plaguebearers
troops.role: Lesser daemons who count every disease in the galaxy.

troops.name: Nurglings
troops.role: Small, mischievous daemon mites.

troops.name: Plague Drones
troops.role: Plaguebearers riding giant Rot Flies.

troops.name: Great Unclean Ones
troops.role: Greater Daemons of Nurgle, massive and jovial.

troops.name: Foetid Bloat-drones
troops.role: Daemon engines that spread plague clouds.

factions.name: Slaanesh
factions.about: The Dark Prince of Excess, Slaanesh is the Chaos God of pleasure, perfection, pride and indulgence. Born from the decadence of the ancient Aeldari, Slaanesh drives followers to push every sensation to its extreme.
lore: Slaanesh was born from the Fall of the Aeldari, an event that shattered their ancient empire.
Slaanesh hungers for Aeldari souls above all others.
The Emperor's Children Legion, led by the Daemon Primarch Fulgrim, serves Slaanesh.
Followers chase perfection and sensation, often ending in madness.
Slaanesh is the youngest of the four great Chaos Gods.
factions.playstyle: Fast, precise and deadly. Slaaneshi forces rely on speed, agility and perfectionist skill, often striking first. In a roleplay setting they suit proud duelists, artists, perfectionists and characters driven by obsession or ego.
goals: Seek perfection in every skill and pursuit
Indulge in ever-greater sensation and experience
Claim the souls of the Aeldari
Rise to daemonhood through excellence

troops.name: Emperor's Children
troops.role: The Traitor Legion devoted to Slaanesh.

troops.name: Noise Marines
troops.role: Chaos Space Marines with sonic weapons.

troops.name: Daemonettes
troops.role: Lesser daemons of Slaanesh, swift and deadly.

troops.name: Seekers
troops.role: Daemonettes riding fast Steeds of Slaanesh.

troops.name: Fiends
troops.role: Scorpion-like daemons that hypnotize their prey.

troops.name: Keepers of Secrets
troops.role: Greater Daemons of Slaanesh, graceful and terrifying.

troops.name: Lord Kakophonist
troops.role: Champion who leads Noise Marines with sound.

troops.name: Cultists of Slaanesh
troops.role: Mortal followers chasing excess.

categories.name: Space Marines
categories.about: The Adeptus Astartes are genetically engineered super-soldiers created by the Emperor of Mankind. Organized into Chapters of around 1,000 warriors, they are the Imperium's finest defenders, sent where the danger is greatest.

factions.name: Adeptus Astartes
factions.about: Each Space Marine is implanted with gene-seed derived from one of the Primarchs, the Emperor's genetically engineered sons. They wear power armor, wield bolters and fight without fear.
lore: The original twenty Space Marine Legions were each led by a Primarch.
During the Horus Heresy, half the Legions turned to Chaos and betrayed the Emperor.
After the Heresy the loyal Legions were broken into smaller Chapters by the Codex Astartes, written by Roboute Guilliman.
Famous Chapters include the Ultramarines, Blood Angels, Dark Angels, Space Wolves and Imperial Fists.
The Primaris Marines, created by Belisarius Cawl, are a newer and stronger generation of Space Marine.
Space Marines receive 19 implanted organs, including a second heart and the Black Carapace that links them to their armor.
factions.playstyle: Elite, well-rounded and adaptable. Space Marines are few in number but extremely durable and skilled, capable of fighting at range or in melee. In a roleplay setting they suit heroic, disciplined and devoted characters who face overwhelming odds with honor.
goals: Defend humanity and the Imperium from all threats
Serve the Emperor and uphold the honor of their Chapter
Destroy xenos, heretics and Chaos
Preserve their gene-seed and Chapter traditions

troops.name: Intercessors
troops.role: Primaris line troops armed with bolt rifles.

troops.name: Tactical Marines
troops.role: Versatile classic Space Marine infantry.

troops.name: Assault Marines
troops.role: Jump-pack troops who strike in melee.

troops.name: Devastator Marines
troops.role: Heavy weapons specialists.

troops.name: Scouts
troops.role: Lightly armored recruits who infiltrate and snipe.

troops.name: Terminators
troops.role: Veterans in heavy Tactical Dreadnought armor.

troops.name: Librarians
troops.role: Psykers who wield the Warp for the Chapter.

troops.name: Chaplains
troops.role: Spiritual leaders who keep the faith and fervor of the Chapter.

troops.name: Apothecaries
troops.role: Medics who recover the gene-seed of fallen Marines.

troops.name: Techmarines
troops.role: Engineers trained by the Adeptus Mechanicus.

troops.name: Dreadnoughts
troops.role: War machines housing mortally wounded heroes.

troops.name: Captains and Chapter Masters
troops.role: Commanders of companies and Chapters.

categories.name: Imperium of Mankind
categories.about: The vast, galaxy-spanning empire of humanity ruled in the name of the God-Emperor, who sits upon the Golden Throne on Terra. It spans over a million worlds and is held together by faith, bureaucracy and endless war.

factions.name: Imperium of Man
factions.about: The Imperium is ruled by the High Lords of Terra and countless institutions, from the Astra Militarum to the Inquisition. Billions of citizens toil and fight to protect humanity from the dangers of the galaxy.
lore: The Emperor has been sustained on the Golden Throne for over ten thousand years after being mortally wounded by Horus.
The Astronomican, a psychic beacon powered by the Emperor, allows ships to navigate the Warp.
The Adeptus Mechanicus of Mars worship the Machine God and maintain the Imperium's technology.
The Inquisition hunts heretics, xenos and daemons, wielding near-absolute authority.
The Great Rift has split the galaxy, cutting the Imperium in half and leaving many worlds in darkness.
Roboute Guilliman has returned as Lord Commander of the Imperium and launched the Indomitus Crusade.
factions.playstyle: Massive numbers, heavy armor and diverse specialists. The Imperium's forces range from simple soldiers to towering Titans, relying on discipline, faith and firepower. In a roleplay setting this is the most flexible faction, suiting soldiers, Inquisitors, priests, tech-priests, rogue traders and ordinary citizens.
goals: Protect humanity from xenos, heretics and Chaos
Serve and worship the God-Emperor
Maintain order and control across the Imperium
Reclaim lost worlds and technology

troops.name: Astra Militarum (Imperial Guard)
troops.role: Billions of human soldiers armed with lasguns.

troops.name: Commissars
troops.role: Officers who enforce discipline and loyalty.

troops.name: Tanks and Artillery
troops.role: Leman Russ battle tanks, Basilisks and Baneblades.

troops.name: Adepta Sororitas (Sisters of Battle)
troops.role: Warrior nuns of the Ecclesiarchy armed with bolters and flamers.

troops.name: Adeptus Mechanicus
troops.role: Tech-priests, Skitarii and robotic war machines from Mars.

troops.name: Imperial Knights
troops.role: Towering walkers piloted by noble houses.

troops.name: Titan Legions
troops.role: Colossal god-machines that dominate the battlefield.

troops.name: Adeptus Custodes
troops.role: The Emperor's golden guardians, even mightier than Space Marines.

troops.name: Inquisitors
troops.role: Agents who hunt threats to humanity.

troops.name: Grey Knights
troops.role: Psychic Space Marines who fight daemons.

troops.name: Officio Assassinorum
troops.role: Elite assassins sent to eliminate key targets.

troops.name: Rogue Traders
troops.role: Explorers who travel beyond the Imperium's borders.
